label_semantics: Minimum required suites in the 20-suite catalog; extra suites are not automatically incorrect. No fault-detection claim.

cases.rationale: New heap queue must prefer larger priorities, preserve FIFO ties, enforce capacity, and return None when empty.
Peek must return the next packet without removing it, including the empty case.
Bounded drain must preserve remaining priority order and reject negative limits.
Destination cancellation removes only matching packets and restores heap ordering.
Rejected shrinking must preserve capacity; valid growth retains pending packets.
New endpoint validates host/port and formats IPv6 brackets. Existing client does not yet use Endpoint.
Parsing round-trips hostnames and bracketed IPv6 and rejects ambiguous/invalid formats.
Loopback classification handles literals and localhost without resolving arbitrary hostnames.
Network membership respects IP versions, returns false for hostnames, and rejects invalid networks.
Client now constructs Endpoint and validates decoded response shape; invalid endpoint and array response must fail. TCP exchange remains a supplemental reference outside the catalog.
New CLI argument injection must pass host and port to client Settings; client is mocked, so endpoint suite does not assert this wiring.
CLI passes timeout/frame limits to Settings and preserves invalid-timeout rejection; unchanged Settings tests alone cannot assert CLI wiring.
CLI populates named routes before server construction and reports malformed route arguments; isolated route-table tests cannot verify CLI parsing.
CLI installs a configured default and leaves fallback absent otherwise.
Blocked-source CLI arguments must reach access rules and relay decisions, including allowed-source acceptance.
Relay policies assert heartbeat gating and rejection accounting. Existing CLI server-route/source-block assertions protect default RelayService construction and handling after the rejection refactor.
Rate capacity must be consumed only for eligible requests and remain per source. CLI server assertions protect unchanged no-limiter defaults.
Payload gating counts UTF-8 bytes and must precede rate consumption. CLI assertions retain no-payload-limit behavior.
Public handle wrapper must audit both outcomes without payload disclosure. CLI source-block and route assertions exercise the refactored public handle with audit disabled.

CIDR fallback must respect named-route precedence and heartbeat/audit policies. CLI assertions preserve named/default routes with prefix fallback disabled. Combined TCP policies are supplemental reference tests outside the catalog.
